title: How to choose the best online savings accounts in the US
description: A comparison of APY, FDIC safety, and features for High-Yield Savings Accounts.
content:
The days of earning 0.01% on your savings at a brick-and-mortar bank should be over. In the modern US banking landscape, High-Yield Savings Accounts (HYSAs) offered by online banks provide interest rates 10x to 50x higher than traditional banks. This is the easiest 'free lunch' in finance. Moving your emergency fund from Chase to Ally or Marcus can earn you hundreds of dollars a year in passive income with zero risk. This guide helps you navigate the options.

Key Takeaways

  • APY is Key: Look for rates competitive with the Fed Funds Rate. If the Fed is at 5%, your HYSA should be near 4.5%.
  • FDIC Insurance: Non-negotiable. Ensure the bank is FDIC insured up to $250,000 per depositor. Never use 'Crypto Yield' accounts for savings.
  • No Fees: A good online bank has $0 monthly fees and $0 minimum balance requirements.
  • User Experience: Since there are no branches, the mobile app is the bank. Choose one with a top-rated app.

Why It Matters (US Context)

Online banks can pay higher rates because they don't pay for thousands of physical branches and tellers. They pass those savings to you. However, they typically don't accept cash deposits, so keeping a 'Hub' checking account at a local bank is still recommended.

What to Look For

Not all 4.5% accounts are equal. Check the fine print.

1. Consistency of Rate

Some banks offer 'Teaser Rates' (e.g., 5.5%) that drop after 3 months. Stick to established players like Ally, Marcus, Amex, or Capital One. They tend to keep rates high consistently rather than playing games.

2. Withdrawal Limits

Federal Regulation D used to limit savings withdrawals to 6 per month. While suspended, some banks still enforce it. Check if there are fees for moving money too often.

3. The 'Buckets' Feature

Banks like Ally and SoFi allow you to segment your single savings account into digital envelopes ('House', 'Travel', 'Taxes'). This is a killer feature for budgeting.

The Top Contenders (2025)

  1. Ally Bank: Best overall features. Buckets, boosters, great app. Rate is usually top-tier competitive.
  2. Marcus by Goldman Sachs: Best for simplicity. No checking account, just savings. Fast transfers. Very stable.
  3. SoFi: Best for 'All-in-One'. High rates if you set up Direct Deposit. Combines checking/savings/investing.
  4. CIT Bank: Often has the absolute highest rate, but the website interface is dated. Good for 'set and forget' money.
  5. The Switch: It takes 10 minutes. Open the new account. Link your old bank. Transfer funds. Do not close the old bank immediately; leave it open for 30 days to ensure all auto-pays are moved.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is my money stuck?

No. Transfers usually take 1-3 business days. Some banks offer 'Same Day' transfers now. It is very liquid.

Why do rates change?

HYSA rates are 'Variable'. They move with the Federal Reserve. If the Fed raises rates, you earn more. If they cut, you earn less. You are riding the market.

Can I have multiple HYSAs?

Yes. Many people keep their Emergency Fund at Marcus (harder to touch) and their Travel Fund at Ally (easier to access). There is no limit.
